title: JCE mathematics: number, algebra and shape
subtitle: Form 2 workbook — the topics that decide a JCE grade

blocks.text: The same quantity can be written three ways, and JCE questions test whether you can move between them without a calculator. Convert a fraction to a decimal by dividing; convert a decimal to a percentage by multiplying by 100. Learn the common ones by heart: one half is 0.5 or 50%, one quarter is 0.25 or 25%, one fifth is 0.2 or 20%.

blocks.label: Worked example 1
blocks.text: A shop reduces the price of a bag of maize from MWK 24 000 by 15%.

Collect like terms before doing anything else. In 5x + 3 - 2x + 7, the x terms give 3x and the numbers give 10, so the expression is 3x + 10. When solving an equation, whatever you do to one side you must do to the other, and undo addition before multiplication.

items: Expand brackets by multiplying every term inside: 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12.
Factorise by taking out the highest common factor: 6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3).
Check a solution by substituting it back into the original equation.
A negative sign in front of a bracket changes every sign inside: -(2x - 5) = -2x + 5.

blocks.text: Area questions usually come down to splitting a shape into rectangles and triangles. Volume is area of cross-section multiplied by length. Write the formula first, substitute, then calculate — the formula line is worth a mark even if the arithmetic goes wrong.

rows: pi x r x r x height

blocks.text: Use 3.14 for pi unless the question gives another value, and keep the units consistent: convert centimetres to metres before multiplying if the answer is asked in square metres.
Underline what the question asks for. 'Calculate the cost' and 'calculate the change' are different answers, and 'give your answer to 2 decimal places' loses a mark when ignored.

items: Show every step: JCE awards method marks, not only the final answer.
Write the units in the answer line: MWK, cm, cm², litres.
If a question says 'hence', it expects you to use your previous answer.
Leave the last two minutes to check that every question has an answer written.
